topics.topic: Canonical identifier scheme for Activation/FlowActivation records so they can be uniquely referenced
questions: What exact stable identifier must represent a FlowActivation record when EffectAttempt.authority points to it?
How is one Activation record uniquely addressed in product records/inspection if Activation has no explicit identifier field?
What concrete identifier is stored and exposed for a flow activation record so other models/actions can reference it deterministically?

quotes:
- `authority`: the approval or the grant it used, or for a `draft-write` send
  the flow activation under which the run started (State 2, A10 rule 6; State
  5) — except a resend after `not_applied`, which, whatever its class, records
  the fresh approval it needed. The authority is named by its identity: an
  approval or a grant by its minted id, a flow activation by its position in
  the store's order (M18), so a version activated again never makes the
  reference ambiguous;

Substitution: fails — each activation is one issued selection; activating the
same implementation again is a new record with its own position in the store's
order (A01 rule 3), not the earlier one.

Substitution: fails — each activation is one issued selection; activating the
same flow version again is a new record with its own position in the store's
order (A01 rule 3), not the earlier one.
judgement.why: State 1 already specifies the uniqueness rule for referencing activation records: their identity is their position in the store’s order.

topics.topic: Agent identity continuity: whether names can be reused and how same-name agents are disambiguated over time
questions: Can an agent name be reused after token revocation/replacement, and if yes how are old vs new agents with the same name distinguished in records?

topics.topic: Authority of State 1: normative source for downstream behavior vs editable draft
questions: Is State 1 normative input for downstream states/code, or only a non-binding draft that can still change model facts and lifecycles?

topics.topic: Cancel/refuse runtime semantics: whether in-progress branch/node executions are aborted or allowed to finish
questions: When cancel/refuse happens while other branches or node attempts are in progress, are those in-progress executions aborted immediately or allowed to conclude (while blocking further sends)?

topics.topic: Deduplication semantics for ContractVersion/Implementation authoring: first-creator metadata retention and no-new-record behavior
questions: When an equal existing contract version or implementation is returned, are `issued_by`/`issued_at` (or `submitted_by`/`submitted_at`) always the first creator metadata, and is no new record written at all?

topics.topic: Definition of map_index for non-mapped nodes and whether it contributes to identity/references
questions: For nodes not mapped over a `many` input, what is `map_index` (absent, null, or a fixed value), and does that choice participate in identity/references?

topics.topic: ManifestOperation identity composition: whether base_url/required_headers/instance_class are identity fields
questions: Are `base_url`, `required_headers`, and `instance_class` part of ManifestOperation identity, even when `record_digest` is unchanged?

topics.topic: Priority rule for EffectAttempt.authority when both EffectApproval and StandingGrant are valid
questions: If both a valid matching approved EffectApproval and an active StandingGrant exist for the same send, which authority must be used and recorded in EffectAttempt?

topics.topic: Value of Slot's current implementation fact when current contract version has no activation/admitted implementation
questions: What is the slot's 'current implementation' fact when the current contract version has no activation yet (e.g., no admitted implementation)?

topics.topic: Whether Run "release" is a formal lifecycle state transition or only metadata on failed runs
questions: Is release a formal lifecycle transition of Run (and if so to what status), or only one-time metadata on a failed run?
